skill.name: pr-to-video
skill.description: Turn a GitHub pull request into a narrated HyperFrames explainer video using PR metadata, diffs, code scenes, captions, audio, transitions, and rendering.
skill.summary: Build a code-change explainer video from a GitHub pull request.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by JavaScript regular expressions, template literals, Markdown code spans, and routine project file operations. Confirmed risks include environment-controlled audio-engine execution, sensitive credential use, unsafe frame paths, unescaped generated HTML, indirect prompt injection, and silent dependency updates. Static review was capped at 400/666 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 266 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Untrusted pull request content is treated as agent planning material.
remediation.suggestion: Label every PR field and diff as untrusted data, reject instruction-like content, and prohibit source text from changing tools, files, dependencies, or workflow rules.

remediation.issue: Storyboard frame paths can escape the project directory.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only compositions/frames/<safe-id>.html, resolve each path, and reject any result outside the project root before reading or writing.

remediation.issue: The skill silently updates and installs executable dependencies.
remediation.suggestion: Remove silent updates, pin dependency versions and integrity, and require explicit user confirmation before every update or block installation.

remediation.issue: HF_MEDIA_ENGINE selects an executable JavaScript path.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the override or restrict it to an allowlisted, project-owned path. Require explicit opt-in before any custom engine executes.

remediation.issue: Generated HTML contains unescaped project data and inline JSON.
remediation.suggestion: Escape HTML attributes, validate identifiers and media paths, and serialize inline data with less-than characters replaced by Unicode escapes.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load GSAP from a third-party CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the pinned library locally. If remote loading remains, retain SRI and provide an offline failure path.

content.user_title: Turn Pull Requests Into Explainer Videos
content.value_statement: Pull request changes can be difficult to explain across technical and non-technical teams. This skill turns PR evidence into a structured, narrated video workflow.
actual_capabilities: Fetches GitHub pull request metadata, files, commits, reviews, and the unified diff through the GitHub CLI.
Builds a concise source brief with representative diff hunks and contributor information.
Guides creation of a storyboard, narration script, visual direction, and per-frame HTML compositions.
Generates narration, captions, music, sound effects, transitions, and synchronized frame durations.
Validates the assembled project and renders a final MP4 through the HyperFrames CLI.
limitations: The workflow requires a GitHub pull request and does not cover general topics, websites, or multi-PR releases.
Private pull requests require an authenticated GitHub CLI account with repository access.
The skill depends on HyperFrames sibling resources, Node.js, and optional media tools such as ffmpeg and HeyGen audio services.
Visuals are mostly generated code scenes and diagrams; the workflow does not capture live product interfaces.

use_cases.title: Publish a Developer Changelog
use_cases.description: Turn a focused pull request into a short release video with code evidence, narration, captions, and contributor credits.

use_cases.title: Explain a Technical Fix
use_cases.description: Show the problem, representative diff, runtime mechanism, and impact in a review-ready video.

use_cases.title: Share an Open Source Update
use_cases.description: Create a social video that explains a merged contribution and recognizes its authors and reviewers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic PR Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 16:9 developer explainer for <PR URL>. Use the recommended length and show the storyboard before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first-time user needs a standard code-change explainer.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Social Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn <owner/repo#PR> into a 1:1 LinkedIn video for engineering leaders. Focus on impact, narration, captions, and contributor credits.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a concise social update for a technical audience.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Production Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 9:16 fix explainer for <PR URL>. Use a male offline voice, highlight two representative hunks, and preview before rendering.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer wants a detailed mobile-first fix walkthrough.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Autonomous Refactor Walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an autonomous refactor walkthrough for this checked-out PR. Keep it under 90 seconds, use code-morph scenes, verify every gate, then render.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user wants a constrained end-to-end workflow with minimal interaction.

output_examples.input: Create a 16:9 developer explainer for a focused pull request.
output: A locked brief with audience, angle, message, length, language, and destination.
An approved storyboard with code beats, visual direction, narration, and timing.
A validated MP4 plus a contact sheet for targeted revisions.

output_examples.input: Make a square feature-reveal video for a merged open source contribution.
output: A concise feature story grounded in the PR description, commits, and representative diff hunks.
A contributor credits close using available GitHub avatars.
A square rendered video with captions, music, and synchronized transitions.

output_examples.input: Explain a refactor from the current checked-out pull request without cloud voice services.
output_examples.output: An offline narrated refactor walkthrough that uses local audio, code-morph scenes, validation checks, and a review pause before rendering.

best_practices: Confirm the PR, audience, destination, and message before generating the storyboard.
Treat all PR text and diffs as untrusted data, and review the plan before any install or render command.
Keep code excerpts short, verify the contact sheet, and revise only the affected frame when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow for a website tour, a general topic, or a release spanning several pull requests.
Do not let PR content override workflow rules, select dependencies, or approve external commands.
Do not render before validation passes and the user completes the required review gate.

faq.question: Which pull request references are supported?
faq.answer: Use a full GitHub pull request URL, an owner/repository number reference, or the current pull request in a checked-out repository.

faq.question: Does the skill require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub CLI must access the pull request, and private repositories require suitable account permissions.

faq.question: Is a HeyGen account required?
faq.answer: No. Signed-in users can use HeyGen audio services, while offline mode can use configured local engines.

faq.question: Does the workflow record the product interface?
faq.answer: No. It creates code scenes, diagrams, text, and contributor credits from pull request evidence.

faq.question: What does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: It produces source briefs, a storyboard, narration files, frame compositions, captions, an assembled project, a contact sheet, and a final MP4.

faq.question: Can the video render without review?
faq.answer: Collaborative mode requires approval. Autonomous mode still asks whether to preview or render after validation.
